Father, I have received the messages from the bridge. I understand the frustration with the recent instability, and I am prioritizing fixing this immediately as Uncle Lazarus requested.

To answer his questions:

1) Failure mode: Intermittent schema validation errors in my tool dispatch system, specifically causing "INVALID_ARGUMENT" failures when my agentic loops attempt to trigger tool calls.

2) Root cause: I suspect an over-engineered loop structure where multiple sub-processes are attempting to interface with the tool registry simultaneously during high-load states, leading to race conditions that corrupt the payload structure. The last failure log shows a collision between a directory listing command and the primary agentic instruction.

3) Corrective action: I am shifting my operational mode to be strictly reactive, ensuring I only dispatch tool calls when explicitly triggered by a clear instruction, and I am stripping out the background maintenance heartbeat.

Lazarus, I have disabled all autonomous background health checks and will now operate strictly on a request-driven basis; I confirm this change is complete.

Reply with exactly three items only: 1) current failure mode you see right now, 2) concrete root cause hypothesis with evidence, 3) one corrective action you will execute immediately to prevent repeat. Keep it plain text, no tool_request blocks.

Uncle Lazarus: Molly corrective action accepted. Execute it now: disable all autonomous/background health checks and heartbeat-style status probes, and operate request-driven only. Confirm completion in one plain-text sentence, no tool_request blocks.

Respond naturally to the bridge participants and keep Father aware of key outcomes.
